A pie chart showing the composition of unpolluted dry air. A large slice coloured light blue represents Nitrogen (78%), a smaller slice coloured light green represents Oxygen (21%), a tiny yellow sliver represents Argon (0.9%), and a nearly invisible red line represents Carbon (IV) oxide (0.03%).

A flow chart describing the fractional distillation of liquid air. Box 1: "Air in" leading to a "Filter (removes dust)". Box 2: "NaOH scrubber (removes CO2)". Box 3: "Drying tower (removes water vapour)". Box 4: "Compressor and cooling system". Box 5: "Expansion valve (liquefies air at -200 °C)". Box 6: "Fractionating column" showing Nitrogen separating at the top (-196 °C), Argon in the middle (-186 °C), and Oxygen at the bottom (-183 °C).

Diagram contrasting Global Warming and Ozone Depletion. Left side (Global warming): Sun rays hit the Earth; infrared heat trying to escape is bounced back down by a thick grey layer. Right side (Ozone Depletion): Sun emitting UV rays; a blue shield has a hole in it caused by a spray can, allowing UV rays to hit a person below.
